question: Can profiles from locally isolated wall states predict a held-out two-wall CA1 response without using target neural rates?

decision.reason: Every held-out deformation row lies outside the row span of the remaining additive wall design. Only two complete local 2x2 wall pairs exist, and both use the same WW target environment, so the neural check cannot establish a portable compositional primitive.

design.training_baseline: square at start of training cycle
design.interaction_free_predictor: (mean WO + mean OW - mean OO) - training square
design.test_target: WW in next cycle - post-test square
design.best_single_comparator: larger target-scored correlation of WO-square and OW-square; an oracle benchmark, not a fitted predictor
design.normalized_rmse: RMSE divided by the RMS of the held-out test residual; no target-fitted intercept or scale
design.predicted_object: registered-cell rate-change vector in the 3x3-bin intersection of two exact-location wall strips

strongest_current_dataset_alternative: Treat the two bit-donut corner queries as a narrow falsification of interaction-free addition, while retaining target-rate-heldout exact-location single-fragment recurrence as the identified reusable-profile analysis. A general compositional test requires new geometries that independently factor wall A and wall B across multiple WW shapes.
